Thompson's group F has no live route tree in the graph. Build one: a decomposition of amenability of F (or of its negation) into prerequisites that can each fail on their own, written as new OPEN claims plus a route, each prerequisite stated precisely and connected to known literature (Moore's Folner function bounds, Kaimanovich's non-Liouville result for F, extensive amenability, Juschenko-Monod). Then attack the most promising prerequisite in full. Wave 4 of this swarm attacked this today: read every dated 2026-09-17 entry under ## Attempts and the nodes they created (git log origin/main --since=12.hours --oneline -- research/), start from where they stopped, and do not repeat their approach.

Attack the negation: that F is NOT amenable. Find the strongest precise sufficient condition (spectral gap of a specific Markov operator, a paradoxical decomposition via the action on dyadic rationals, a cost or l2-invariant, a uniform lower bound on cogrowth) and either prove it or prove exactly where every member of that class dies. Record the obstruction as a claim. Decomposition via weak containment: Bernoulli shifts are weakly contained in every free action (Abert-Weiss), and cost is upper semicontinuous under weak containment (Kechris). Fixed price is then equivalent to a precise lower-semicontinuity statement. Write that decomposition as claims and routes if not already present (bin/cairn search), and attack the lower-semicontinuity statement on the widest class you can.
